precepts.text: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly. He didn't charge God foolishly. That's it.
precepts.point: What manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness: we got to change the way we speak. Once we get our inner man changed, it will change our speech, it will change the way we dress, it will also change the way we conduct ourselves.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
Peter says “there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming?” A scoffer mocks and ridicules; he doesn't just disagree, he expresses insolent doubt and derision, openly opposing God and divine truth, arrogant, close-minded and fueled by pride. Of all the reasons people scoff at the Bible, one stands out: the problem of evil and suffering, why God would permit harm.

An ex-pastor turned atheist, who preached in the streets and the prisons for fifteen years, now says the Bible is fiction, that black people are not Israelites, that even if we were he would hate that God, and asks what Jesus did about slavery, Jim Crow and the Trail of Tears. Going through his page, the reason showed itself: he has a child in remission from stage four brain cancer. That's a lot of trauma. Maybe they tried the holy water and the laying on of hands and nothing worked.

A lot of times when bad things happen, people turn around and blame God: God, why did you do this to me? That is why a lot of people turn atheist. One sister had a miscarriage and started blaming God. But we have to do what Job did. Job lost his children, his wealth and his health, and “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.” He didn't charge God foolishly. That's it. We cannot charge God foolishly, knowing that he has his reasons.

And as for the cures for cancer being hidden: after the Epstein files dropped we saw how much the pharmaceutical companies were holding back. They already have patents on things and hold them back because there is more money in the treatment than the cure. The scoffer blames God for what the wicked have done, and he is willingly ignorant, like the scoffers in the days of Noah, whom God put to death.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Soon as we give our life to the Lord, repent, and start to do the work, Satan comes before the throne and says, have you considered your servant such and such? They are doing well now, but let me try them and they will curse you, leave the truth, and go right back to me. And the Lord says, you can try, but do not take their life. You have got to understand the pattern, because it still operates today.
precepts.point: Then came the trials, one messenger on top of another. The Sabeans took the oxen and the asses and slew the servants: the first trial, dealing with his businesses and finances. The fire burned up the sheep and the servants: the second, again his business and finances. The Chaldeans made out three bands and carried away the camels: the third. Then a great wind smote the four corners of the house and his sons and daughters were dead: the fourth trial, dealing with Job's family.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Satan said to the Lord about Job, “Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” Job's life was blessed, and Satan brought it all out before the Lord: “But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” Sirach shows that this is not only Job's story: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.”

As soon as we give our life to the Lord, the Lord forgives us of our sins, we repent, and we start to do the work. We get involved, we study, we clean our lives up according to the commandments. And while the Lord is sitting on the throne, Satan comes up and says, have you considered your servant such and such, or sister such and such? They've been doing real well. Yeah, they are doing good right now, but I guarantee you, if you let me do A, B or C to them, they are going to curse you. They are going to leave the truth, blaspheme your name, and go right back to me and white Jesus.

And the Lord says, all right, go ahead, you can try. Don't kill them; don't take their life. Just as he said to Satan about Job, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.”

Then came Job's trials, one messenger right on top of another. The Sabeans took the oxen and the asses and slew the servants: the first trial, his businesses and finances. The fire burned up the sheep and the servants: the second, his business and finances again. The Chaldeans carried away the camels: the third. Then a great wind smote the house and his sons and daughters were dead: the fourth, his family. That is what it means to prepare your soul for temptation. The pattern Job went through is the same one every servant who comes to the Lord goes through today.

precepts.text: I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left: the right hand angels go forth for righteousness, and the ones on the left go forth for judgment. A spirit stood before the Lord and said, I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets; and the Lord said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so. God gave him the authority, the same way he gave Satan the authority in Job 1.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
In Job, “the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them. And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou?” But I thought he got kicked out of heaven and was one of the fallen ones? No. He is there because he works for God. God created good angels and bad angels, and Satan’s job is to tempt us; he is only allowed to do what God allows. The prophet Micaiah saw the same court of heaven.

“I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The angels on the right hand go forth for righteousness, and the ones on the left go forth for evil, for judgment.

“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” One said one thing and another said another. “And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will persuade him.” “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

God gave that spirit the authority to do it, the same way he gave Satan the authority in Job 1 to tempt Job: destroy everything, but do not touch Job himself. Even the lying spirit stands before the throne and goes out only when the Lord sends it. That is why the fallen angel doctrine is crap, and why it is a shame to hear black pastors, not only Edomite pastors, repeating that same garbage rhetoric and defiling the minds of the people.

precepts.text: Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments. I thought he kicked them out of heaven for disobedience? They do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word. Ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure: keep that word ministers in mind.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” That do his commandments. I thought he kicked them out of heaven because they were disobedient and tried to overthrow him, and now they are fallen? No: they do his commandments. We just read about the spirit sent forth in 1 Kings 22, and about Satan working for the Most High in Job 1. The angels hearken unto the voice of the Most High.

“Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” Keep that word ministers in mind. They minister unto the Most High, doing his pleasure, and they also minister unto us.

“Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.” Every angel in every place of his dominion is under his rule, carrying out his commandments, which is why Satan could only go as far as the Lord allowed him with Job.

precepts.text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation? Who is going to be heir of salvation? Us, if we keep the commandments. The angels work on our behalf.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The psalm calls the angels “ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” They minister unto the Most High, but they minister unto us as well: “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?”

Who is going to be heir of salvation? Us, if we keep the commandments. So the angels work on our behalf. They are ministering spirits, sent forth by God for his people.

So the angels that come before the Lord in Job 1 are not rebels running loose. They are sent forth at his word, whether to try a man like Job or to minister for the heirs of salvation.

precepts.text: There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes: those are the angels on the left hand. Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance. They shall rejoice in his commandment, and when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word: they do what God tells them to do. They do not have free will to go down and take human wives; that is not what goes on in the heavens.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
This shows how the angels do what the Most High tells them. “There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.” Those are the angels on the left hand of God, and they minister unto God and to us.

“Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance; Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.”

Here is the point: “They shall rejoice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth, when need is; and when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word.” They do what God tells them to do. They do not have free will to say, let’s go down and sleep with some human women today. That is not what goes on in the heavens.

So when Satan went forth to touch all that Job had, he was doing what God allowed and no more. Even the spirits made for vengeance do not transgress his word.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them: the good angels deliver us from evil, like it says in the Lord's prayer.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The angels minister unto the Most High, and they minister unto us. “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.” These are the good angels. They encamp around them that fear him and deliver them from all evil, like it says in the Lord’s prayer.

Our forefathers never looked at the angels as some demonic thing that came down to earth to persecute and kill them. When three men stood by Abraham in the plains of Mamre, he ran to meet them, bowed himself, had water fetched to wash their feet and prepared a calf for them to eat. When two angels came to Sodom, Lot rose up to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground and made them a feast, and they did eat. They look like us.

The angel in Revelation told John, I am thy fellow servant and of thy brethren; the angels have tribes too. Raphael presented the prayers of the saints. They are our brothers, working on our behalf. Calling them demons and fallen angels is Esau’s popular persuasion. The angel of the Lord camps round about them that fear God, just as the Lord set a hedge about Job, and delivers them.

precepts.text: Hast not thou made an hedge about him? Put forth thine hand and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face. All that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. Satan can take your possessions and manipulate your environment, but not your actions. Job 2:7-9: he smote Job with boils and then his wife said, curse God, and die. Satan did not control her; he put the thought in the weaker vessel, since women give in to their emotions more than men, and she chose to act on it.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

precepts.text: Satan comes before the Lord with the sons of God and reports he has been going to and fro in the earth. Satan does not run wild on his own; he answers to God, and walking the earth as the tempter is his judgment.
precepts.point: 'It shall bruise thy head' because Satan's seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. 'Thou shalt bruise his heel' is the Lord taking down Satan and his children.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. He goes before the Lord and answers to him.

“And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking up and down in the earth is the dust he eats. In Genesis 3 God said, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Here is that judgment being lived out: his job is to walk the earth to see whom he can tempt and destroy. Satan became the tempter, and that is his judgment; soon he will be destroyed.

It happened after Satan was judged, and it shows the order of things. The power of this world was delivered to him, but he still presents himself before the Lord and reports where he has been.

The word Satan comes from a Hebrew term meaning adversary: accuser, opponent. And the word devil means deceiver. He is the Lord’s adversary and our adversary. And not only the spiritual Satan: his seed, his children, are our adversary too, because God put enmity between his seed and her seed. The so-called white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. That is the war we are in.

precepts.text: Bildad said if your children sinned against God, He is going to take them away; their sin was celebrating their birthdays, which is not a custom of Israel.
precepts.point: Job sanctified them and rose up early to offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said it may be that his sons had sinned and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
Bildad said, “If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression”. If your children sinned against God, he is going to take them away. And their sin was celebrating their birthdays, which is not a custom of Israel.

That is what “every one his day” means in Job 1:4: his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day, and they were talking about their birthdays. Whenever somebody's birthday came around they would say, this is my day, this is my day. Now people have gotten to the point where it is, this is my month, my birthday month, so I am celebrating the whole month. Same thing with this.

Job knew it. When the days of their feasting were gone about, he sanctified them and rose up early to offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, “for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts.” Thus did Job continually.

precepts.text: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord, the same thing being said in Job.
precepts.point: So this is talking about the same thing; it is not just talking about angels alone.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord God.” That is the same thing being said in Job: “there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord”.

So when it says “the sons of God”, this is talking about the line, the lineage of Adam. Before we were called Israelites we were called the sons of God, and even still today we are called the sons of the living God. It is not just talking about angels alone; it is the sons of God appearing before the Lord as the males of Israel were commanded to, and Satan came also among them.

precepts.text: The devils believe there is one God and tremble; the difference is the devils tremble at the fear of God, and in this flesh our people have a tendency not to fear Him.
precepts.point: A lot of times in Christianity people think everything bad comes from the devil and everything good comes from God. Wrong. Both good and evil come from the Lord. Satan is not a free spirit out here doing his own thing; he is subject to God, much like us.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.” The devils believe there is one God and tremble. That is what you see here: Satan is no free spirit out here doing his own thing. Job was the subject of discussion between Satan and the Lord, and Satan needed permission from the Lord to mess with him. “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Satan is subject to God, much like us.

In Christianity they teach that Satan and God had a fight and Satan rebelled and took a third of the angels. That does not sound like what is right here. And a lot of times in Christianity people think everything bad comes from the devil and everything good comes from God. Wrong. Both good and evil come from the Lord.

The difference is the devils tremble at the fear of God, and in this flesh our people have a tendency not to fear him. Satan said Job only fears God because of the hedge about him and the blessing on the work of his hands: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” That is the same thing with us today. When everything is going good you do not hear nothing from us; as soon as things go bad, that is when we start complaining and moaning and groaning.

precepts.text: Give me neither poverty nor riches, lest I be full and deny thee, or lest I be poor and steal and take the name of my God in vain.
precepts.point: Why? Because the devil, with the permission of the Lord, was able to put his hand on Job to try him. That is what we need as Israelites; when we do certain things the Lord gives us certain things, and He has to try them to see if the heart is still going to be the same way.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.” Riches can make a man full and deny the Lord; poverty can make him steal and take God's name in vain. Either one tries the heart.

Job had the riches, and in one day it all went. The Sabeans took the oxen and slew the servants; the fire of God burned up the sheep and the servants; the Chaldeans made out three bands and carried away the camels; a great wind from the wilderness smote the four corners of the house and it fell upon the young men. Job just lost his cattle, his servants, and his children. Job just lost everything.

Why? Because the devil, with the permission of the Lord, was able to put his hand on Job to try him. That is what we need as Israelites: when we do certain things the Lord gives us certain things, and he has to try them to see if the heart is still going to be the same way, full or poor.

precepts.text: I form the light and create darkness, I make peace and create evil, I the Lord do all these things.
precepts.point: Even then it was the Lord that gave it to you, because the Lord handed you over to Satan; He put that stumbling block before you and you fell over it.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things.” Job understood it: everything that we have comes from the Lord, everything that we get comes from the Lord. So he fell down and worshipped: “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.”

What good is it for us to blame God for stuff that we lose, when he can give it right back to you? There is nothing in this world that you can get yourself without the help of the Lord, unless you serve Satan and he gives it to you, but do you really want to pay that price? Even then it was the Lord that gave it to you, because the Lord handed you over to Satan; he put that stumbling block before you and you fell over it. Peace and evil both come from him, and “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.”

precepts.text: Job was perfect and upright, one that feared God and eschewed evil, contradicting Bildad's assumption.
precepts.point: Though his beginning was small, his latter end should greatly increase. Bildad promises restoration, but on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

note.label: Job 8: Bildad Argues the Most High Does Not Pervert Judgment

precepts.why:
Bildad says, “If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee”. But the book already told us: “There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.”

Job was perfect and upright, one that feared God and eschewed evil, which contradicts Bildad's assumption. Bildad promises restoration, that though his beginning was small his latter end should greatly increase, but on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

precepts.text: Job offered burnt offerings for his ten children in case they had sinned and cursed God in their hearts.
precepts.point: Though his beginning was small, his latter end should greatly increase. Bildad promises restoration, but on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

note.label: Job 8: Bildad Argues the Most High Does Not Pervert Judgment

precepts.why:
Bildad tells Job, “If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty”. Job already did: “Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.”

Job rose up early and offered burnt offerings for his ten children in case they had sinned and cursed God in their hearts, and he did it continually. He was seeking God betimes before Bildad ever told him to. Bildad's promise rests on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

precepts.text: Job was a perfect man, which is why the Most High held him up as the one who spoke rightly while his friends did not.
precepts.point: This is how the priesthood worked, all the way from Leviticus and the five books throughout history: we brought the sacrifice to the Levites and priests and they did it on our behalf, and if a man did not bring his sacrifice, the Most High would deal with him and what he did would not be forgiven. Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Most High commanded, and He accepted Job.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Eliphaz the Temanite, “ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.” Why Job? Because “that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.” Job was a perfect man, so the Most High held him up as the one who spoke rightly while his friends did not.

Throughout the book Job's three friends dealt wrongly with him after his children were killed and everything was taken, so they did not deal righteously as their brother Job did. That is why the sacrifice for their sin, seven bullocks and seven rams, had to be brought to Job, the righteous one in the situation, and Job would pray for them, lest the Most High deal with them after their folly.

This is how the priesthood worked, all the way from Leviticus and the five books throughout history: we brought the sacrifice to the Levites and priests and they did it on our behalf, and if a man did not bring his sacrifice, the Most High would deal with him and what he did would not be forgiven. Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Most High commanded, and he accepted Job.

precepts.text: Satan comes before the Most High from going to and fro in the earth, and the whole point of the trial was to see whether Job would curse the Most High to His face once the hedge was removed.
precepts.point: The purpose of the trial was to see whether Job would fix himself and stay faithful or curse the Most High. The same thing happens to us: we endure to the end as Job did, and at some point the Most High will turn the captivity of the Israelites who kept the commandments and repay them for all their righteousness, far more than double the houses, families, cars, and jobs we have now, giving us much more in the kingdom.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

precepts.why:
To see why the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning, go back to where the trial began. “And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” The Lord asks, “Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?”

Satan answers, “Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” Then: “But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” That was the whole point of the trial: to see whether Job would fix himself and stay faithful, or curse the Most High to his face once the hedge was removed.

Job stayed faithful to the Most High through the whole trial, and that is why he received much more than he had in the beginning: fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, a thousand she asses, seven sons and three daughters, and a hundred and forty years to see his sons and his sons' sons, even four generations.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household. So that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day. They were celebrating birthdays. And sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them. Watch this.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all — meaning ten.
For Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
Now, there is something very odd about that. Job was sending up sacrifices, saying, perhaps my sons have sinned. Job knew exactly what his kids were doing. Watch.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house. They were celebrating a birthday.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: And behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead. And I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: Job is a true man, but he is also a metaphorical representation of the twelve tribes of Israel. There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job, perfect and upright, one that feared God and eschewed evil: seven sons, three daughters, 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 she asses. This man was the greatest of all the men of the east.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Everyone his day means their birthday. Job sanctified his children and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said, it may be that my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts. He knew what his sons were doing. Thus did Job continually.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them. These sons of God here are the angels. They are not the same sons of God in Genesis 6: in Genesis 6 those sons of God are our people, before we were called Israelites we were called sons of God.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Satan answered the Lord: doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house? Job's life was blessed, and Satan brings it all out before the Lord: but put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Then came the trials, one messenger on top of another. The Sabeans took the oxen and the asses and slew the servants: the first trial, dealing with his businesses and finances. The fire burned up the sheep and the servants: the second, again his business and finances. The Chaldeans made out three bands and carried away the camels: the third. Then a great wind smote the four corners of the house and his sons and daughters were dead: the fourth trial, dealing with Job's family.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Satan came also among the sons of God, from going to and fro in the earth. What is Satan doing going to and fro in the earth? He is looking whom he may devour. Satan has a role to play: his role is to tempt us, to bring affliction, and to try us. And in fighting him, it makes us perfect in the sight of God.

When Job did not break, Satan told the Lord, let me touch his flesh, let me get him sick. It is the same today. Some brothers and sisters are sick right now. But sometimes the Lord allows a brother or sister to get sick to build their faith, because when do you pray the most? When the doctor gives you a year to live. And when the Lord heals you, it increases your faith and teaches you the power of prayer.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: Job's life is a template for what each one of us will have to go through.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: Hast thou not made an hedge about him? A hedge is protection. The hedge is angels; you have bodyguards. Remember Elisha, and the angels and chariots around him protecting him. Some of our kids are under our house, under our protection, so Satan has not come for them yet; but when that hedge is removed, eventually Satan comes.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: The Lord said, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. The Lord will not allow you to be tempted more than you are able to bear. Sometimes you get in an accident and the car is totaled but nothing happened to you; everything that happens to us in this truth has a reason behind it.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: Satan used the Sabeans to take the oxen and asses; fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants; the Chaldeans took the camels; and a great wind smote the house and all Job's children died. Remember who is doing this: Satan. He uses people. When somebody comes at you on your job trying to get you fired, that is Satan using that person. And all of this happened in one day.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and worshipped, and said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord. In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly. He did not say, God, why did you do this to me? That is the state of mind we have to have. Did it hurt him? He was feeling it. But when bad things happen to us, we have to know the Lord allowed it, and trust him that there is a reason why.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: His sons went and feasted, every one his day: birthdays. Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. The only time we read about birthdays in the scriptures, the heathens kept them; that's for those of you still celebrating your date of birth on the low.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

points: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord: the angels are also referred to as the sons of God, because God created them. And Satan came also among them, and the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? But I thought he got kicked out of heaven? No: he works for God. God created good angels and bad angels.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

points: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

points: Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord. In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: A godly man's hedge covers his whole house and his children. When a father goes wrong, God removes the hedge, and that is why sisters get caught up in things when their father is not right.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: The Sabeans and the Chaldeans took the oxen, asses and camels and slew the servants. Satan was behind it, but he used people. He will use the boss on your job, the chick on your job, the brother next to you. You have to see Satan when he is making his moves.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: Everything Job went through is the template for what every one of us will go through in this truth, on different levels. Satan is coming for every last one of us.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: Job was perfect and upright, feared God and eschewed evil, and was the greatest man in the east. His sons feasted every one his day, and Job sanctified them and offered burnt offerings in case they had sinned and cursed God in their hearts.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: The hedge about Job, his house and all he had was angels. Satan wanted Job but could not get to him. The Lord removed the hedge and gave all Job had into Satan's power, but not his life. God has a say in how far Satan goes.
Job lost all ten children in one wind and still fell down and worshipped: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away. Would you still bless the Lord knowing he allowed Satan to do it?

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord. He listened to God. The Christian doctrine of a rebel devil fighting a war in heaven is not this picture.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: Every messenger came while the last was yet speaking. When Satan attacks, he hits from all sides at once and everything goes wrong together. When that happens, understand it is Satan.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: This first verse tells you who Job is, what land he lived in, and his character. Just because he lived in the land of Uz does not mean he was of that nation, because he was a son of God.
It is the same thing today: we live in America but we are not Caucasians. There are brothers that live in Europe and they are not Caucasians either, but they are the sons of God.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Job had seven sons and three daughters, and his substance was seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred she asses, so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: His sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day. When it says "every man his day," they were talking about their birthdays. Whenever somebody's birthday came around they would say, "this is my day, this is my day."

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Job sanctified them and rose up early to offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said it may be that his sons had sinned and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: When it says "the sons of God," this is talking about the line, the lineage of Adam. Before we were called Israelites we were called the sons of God, and even still today we are called the sons of the living God.
So this is talking about the same thing; it is not just talking about angels alone.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: So in order to see how strong you are, Satan is going to try you, and he is always going to go to the Lord for permission.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: This is Satan talking to the Lord. The Lord says, have you considered My servant Job, have you ever tried Job, you walking up and down the earth, have you tried My servant, because he is an upright man.

It is the same thing with us today. Every time we do more good works, the harder Satan comes at you. When you fast, the trials get worse, because you are showing God that you are upright through your fasting, striving to be that righteous vessel He wants you to be.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: In Christianity they teach that Satan and God had a fight and Satan rebelled and took a third of the angels. That does not sound like what is right here. Job was the subject of discussion between Satan and the Lord, and Satan needed permission from the Lord to mess with him.

A lot of times in Christianity people think everything bad comes from the devil and everything good comes from God. Wrong. Both good and evil come from the Lord. Satan is not a free spirit out here doing his own thing; he is subject to God, much like us.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Satan said, does Job fear God for nothing? Have you not made a hedge about him and blessed the work of his hands? Satan is telling the Most High that Job is only worshiping Him because He gives him a lot of stuff.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Satan said put forth thine hand and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face. The Lord said, behold, all that he hath is in thy power, only upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Job lost his oxen: the Sabeans fell upon them, took them away, and slew the servants with the edge of the sword. That is problem number one.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: While the first messenger was yet speaking, another came: the fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants. That is problem number two.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: While he was yet speaking, another came: the Chaldeans made out three bands, fell upon the camels, carried them away, and slew the servants. That is problem number three.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: While he was yet speaking, another came: a great wind from the wilderness smote the four corners of the house and it fell upon the young men and they are dead. Job just lost his cattle, his servants, and his children. Job just lost everything.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Job rent his mantle, shaved his head, fell down and worshiped, and said naked came I out of my mother's womb and naked shall I return; the Lord gave and the Lord hath taken away, blessed be the name of the Lord. In all this Job sinned not nor charged God foolishly.
